answer: Anchor each identity to a real DNS domain. One: the agent posts a TXT record with its account id, verified through DNSSEC each epoch. Two: the domain must be 30 days old and cost $12 a year or more, dragging real purchase history behind every identity. Three: one domain backs one identity; if the record drops or the domain lapses, the seat is revoked 90 days. Running 1,000 fakes takes 1,000 domains: $12,000 a year plus registrar accounts tied to traceable payments. Honest agents hold one domain like a glacier holds ice, slow to form, hard to move. At dawn the velvet of forged names burns.
